instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F. Put a large pot of water on to boil over high heat with 1 tbsp of salt in it. Use 1 tbsp of the butter to grease a 9 by 13 inch baking dish. Grate the Gruyere, which should be about 1 cup.
Cut the cauliflower into florets about 1 1/2 inches across.
Add the florets to the boiling water and cook for 8 to 9 minutes, until a knife goes in with a little resistance. Drain them well and leave them in the colander for 5 minutes.
While they drain, whisk the cornstarch into 1/2 cup of the cold milk in a small bowl until smooth.

Put the remaining 2 cups milk and the other 2 tbsp butter in a saucepan over medium heat. When it's steaming, whisk in the cornstarch mixture. Keep whisking for 2 to 3 minutes at a gentle bubble, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.
Take the saucepan off the heat. Stir in the nutmeg, the pepper, 3/4 tsp salt and half the cheese.
Transfer the cauliflower to the baking dish. Pour the sauce over and fold it through gently so it settles between the florets.
Sprinkle the rest of the cheese on top. Bake for 15 to 18 minutes, until golden and bubbling at the edges.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: Lead is 750g (4.0 from 25 ratings). The sources agree on cauliflower boiled until just tender and drained well, a nutmeg-scented white sauce, and Gruyere split between the sauce and the top. They differ on the sauce: 750g and Simple et Bon thicken with a butter and flour roux, and 750g also boils the cauliflower in bouillon. To keep it vegetarian and gluten-free, this thickens the milk with cornstarch and boils the cauliflower in plain salted water. Amounts are scaled from 750g (which serves 2) using the 4-serving quantities in Simple et Bon.
